description: Curated map from proof target to the ACL2 events that support it. This file is edited by hand and is the only hand-edited half of the ledger; tools/ledger.py checks every name against the books and regenerates the events arrays of planning/proofs.json from it. A name here must exist, must not be flagged SUSPECT by the shape detector, and must live in a book the Makefile certification roots reach. A pending_subject note records that the theorem is about a function the host does not call, so the citation does not yet meet the "theorem subject is the function the host calls" rule.

events.name: fn-wire-feed-proper-append
events.pending_subject: Subject is fn-wire-feed-proper; the host calls fn-wire-next (host/reader-host.lisp:91) and no theorem equates them. Review section 4, wire row.

events.name: fn-stx-durable-completion-is-an-acceptance
events.note: The subject-equating theorem AGENTS.md rule 1 asks for, for the preservation half of this target: fn-stx-index-invariant-preserved-by-accept hypothesises fn-stx-acceptedp, and this proves fn-stx-acceptedp of the durable branch of fn-node-complete with the accepted article named. The host line is host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-finish -> fn-sn-finish (books/store-node.lisp) -> that call.

events.name: fn-sn-finish-preserves-indexedp
events.note: The carrier obligation, and the one preservation row that does work: the store grows at fn-sn-finish by the one article fn-install-pending conses and the carried index grows by that article's delta, at most one cons. Its keystone is fn-stx-index-invariant-preserved-by-accept and its hypothesis is discharged by fn-stx-durable-completion-is-an-acceptance. 11,118 prover steps. Decision D21.

events.name: fn-sn-statement-lookup-is-the-lace-lookup
events.note: The subject-equating theorem AGENTS.md rule 1 asks for, for the QUERY half. Subject: fn-sn-statement-lookup (books/store-node.lisp), which host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-statement calls on the 'fn-store-sn global, reachable from outside as run_store.py statement --id. Its hypothesis fn-sn-indexedp holds of that global by a reachability chain: fn-sn-initial-is-indexed and the preservation theorems for prepare, io, finish, crash, recover and set-keyring (books/store-node-invariants), refuse-reservation and known-abort (books/store-node-resolution), open-observed (books/store-observed) and the sweep, which returns the store unchanged. The one site not covered is host/bp-ingress-host.lisp, whose fn-bpi-ingress-prepare has no such theorem; it is recorded open. :rule-classes nil so it cannot rewrite the cheap query back into the linear projection.

events.name: fn-peer-ihave-of-a-held-message-id-is-435-and-no-article
events.note: The subject-equating theorem AGENTS.md rule 1 asks for, on the duplicate-offer row. The host line is host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk -> books/owner.lisp fn-own-read -> fn-served-step -> fn-served-dispatch -> fn-auth-step -> fn-peer-step -> fn-peer-command, whose IHAVE and CHECK arms are the only callers of fn-peer-decide-offer on this tree. It says the reply octets ARE that decision and that no article mode is entered, so a duplicate offer costs the peer no bytes.

events.note: The subject-equating theorem AGENTS.md rule 1 asks for, on the duplicate-offer row. The host line is host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk -> books/owner.lisp fn-own-read -> fn-served-step -> fn-served-dispatch -> fn-auth-step -> fn-peer-step -> fn-peer-command, whose IHAVE and CHECK arms are the only callers of fn-peer-decide-offer on this tree. It says the reply octets ARE that decision and that no article mode is entered, so a duplicate offer costs the peer no bytes.

events.name: fn-own-read-offers-against-the-live-node
events.note: The other half of the same bridge: WHICH node the served path hands fn-peer-decide-offer. Until w11/transit-correct it was the value fn-peer-open-session pinned at :open, so the duplicate refusal was unreachable on a live connection and the wire answered 335 and 238 (V0-TRANSIT-DUPLICATE and V0-TRANSIT-CHECK-DUP at 6fb30ca). fn-own-conn-live-session re-pins it from the owner's store once per socket read.

events.name: fn-own-live-session-boundedp
events.note: The re-pin cannot drop a connection: it leaves the reader session identical, so fn-own-conn-boundedp -- the test fn-own-read applies after the step, and the one that made ADVANCE a silent no-op for a wave when a rebuild lost a wrapper -- answers exactly as before.

events.name: fn-hsig-subject-body-injective

The body is called by fn-hsig-signed-preimage, reached through host/hybrid-signature-host.lisp fn-hsig-host-preimage and host/native/signatures.lisp. Certified with concrete hypothesis counterexamples in run certify-20260921T181329Z-2345431; all source digests match the integration tree. No primitive-security claim.

events.name: fn-hsig-signed-preimage-injective
events.note: Combines subject-body projection injectivity with crypto-seam tagged-preimage injectivity for the actual fn-hsig-host-preimage signing subject, under two well-formed-subject hypotheses. Certified in run certify-20260921T181329Z-2345431; no claim about signature security.

events.name: fn-auth-step-binds-a-peer-role-only-by-a-principal-login
events.note: The only way in, over fn-auth-step (books/served.lisp fn-served-dispatch; host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk via fn-own-read and fn-served-step). Two hypotheses (unbound before, bound after), each with a must-fail and a refuting value in tests/acl2/nntp-auth-teeth-tests.lisp keystone 8.

events.name: fn-auth-step-principal-login-binds-exactly-the-unique-match
events.note: The way in, over fn-auth-step: an accepted AUTHINFO PASS is 281, installs the principal and binds exactly fn-auth-principal-match (nil for a mismatch or a duplicate). Eleven hypotheses, each with a must-fail and a refuting value (teeth keystone 9).

events.name: fn-auth-step-starttls-clears-a-principal-role
events.note: The way out, over fn-auth-step: entering the TLS handshake drops the subject, the cached name and a principal-derived role and keeps a source-address role. Two hypotheses, each with a must-fail and a refuting value (teeth keystone 10).

events.name: fn-ocfg-open-begins-unbound
events.note: Over fn-ocfg-open, which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-open calls: an accepted open installs a reader with no role, subject, cached name, TLS layer or handshake, whatever the owner's other connections did. One hypothesis with a must-fail; witness and refuting value in tests/acl2/owner-config-tests.lisp.
